title: Library volunteer
scenario: You are a new volunteer at a college library. A librarian is showing you how to help visitors.
sentences: Please welcome visitors at the front desk.
Show them where the quiet study rooms are.
Visitors with a student card can borrow up to five books.
If a book is late, please ask the visitor to pay a fee.
The printers on the second floor are free for all students.
Anyone looking for old newspapers should ask the basement librarian.
Remind everyone to return their books before the library closes.

title: Campus café trainee
scenario: You are a new worker at the campus café. The manager is explaining the rules of the job.
sentences: Always wash your hands before starting work.
Greet every customer with a smile.
Write each order clearly on a card and give it to the cook.
Please keep the counter clean and put the cups back on the shelf.
If a customer has an allergy, ask the manager first.
The coffee machine must be turned off and cleaned at the end of every evening.
On busy days, you can take a short break after you finish the lunch rush.

title: Dormitory helper
scenario: You are a student helper at a dormitory. A resident advisor is training you to welcome new students.
sentences: Give each new student a key and a folder.
Show them where the laundry room is located.
Remind them that visitors must leave the building by ten o'clock.
The kitchen on each floor is shared by all of the residents.
If students lose their keys, they should contact the front office right away.
Please tell them that the heating in every room can be controlled with the small dial.
Students who need help with their luggage can ask a volunteer wearing a green badge.

title: Laboratory safety
scenario: You are assisting in a chemistry laboratory. A teaching assistant is explaining the safety rules.
sentences: Always wear your safety glasses in the lab.
Tie back your hair before you begin.
Never taste or smell any of the chemicals in the lab.
If something spills, tell your instructor and leave the area.
Put used glass into the special box, not into the trash.
After class, wash your hands and return all equipment to the correct shelf.
Students who have long sleeves should roll them up so they do not touch the burners.

title: Science museum guide
scenario: You are a volunteer guide at a college science museum. A coordinator is training you to talk to visitors.
sentences: Welcome the visitors to the museum.
Explain how to use the exhibits.
The dinosaur exhibit is located on the second floor.
Young children must always be accompanied by an adult.
Please ask visitors not to touch the fragile glass cases.
The gift shop near the exit sells books, posters, and small science kits for children.
If you cannot answer a question, politely suggest asking a staff member.

title: International student ambassador
scenario: You are a student ambassador at the international office. A staff member is training you to give advice to new students.
sentences: Check your university email daily.
Bring your passport and visa to the office.
The campus bank offers special accounts for new students.
Students can join a conversation group to practice speaking English.
If you have questions about classes, visit your advisor.
You must register for all of your courses online before the first week ends.
Many students visit the writing center, where tutors review their essays.

title: Psychology survey assistant
scenario: You are a student assistant in a psychology department. A professor is explaining how to run a short survey.
sentences: Please greet each participant politely.
Explain that the survey is voluntary.
Participants should sign a consent form before the survey begins.
The questionnaire takes about fifteen minutes to complete.
If someone feels uncomfortable, they may stop at any time.
After each session, thank the participant and write the date in the notebook.
Please keep all the finished answer sheets in the locked cabinet every evening.

title: Campus tour guide
scenario: You are leading a campus tour for prospective students. A tour manager is reviewing what to say at each stop.
sentences: Begin by introducing yourself.
The library is open until midnight.
The science building has modern laboratories for students.
Most first-year students live in the residence halls near the sports center.
Lunch is served in the dining hall from eleven thirty until two.
Students can join one of over a hundred clubs that meet in the union.
Questions about applying can be sent to the admissions office directly.

title: Conference volunteer
scenario: You are volunteering at an academic conference. The organizer is explaining your responsibilities.
sentences: Please check each guest's name badge carefully.
Direct guests to the registration desk.
Speakers must arrive early to test their presentation equipment.
Lunch is provided for registered participants only.
The poster session takes place in the east wing of the building.
Anyone having difficulty hearing should be directed to the front seats.
If a technical problem occurs, tell the coordinator right away.

title: Student newspaper intern
scenario: You are an intern at the student newspaper. An editor is explaining how to prepare for an interview.
sentences: Research your subject thoroughly beforehand.
Prepare questions that need detailed answers.
Always ask permission before recording a conversation.
Listen closely, since good questions often follow answers.
Take notes by hand as well, in case the recording does not work.
Afterward, send a brief message to thank the person and confirm the quotations.
Every claim in an article should be supported by a reliable source.

title: Water-testing project
scenario: You are a research assistant in an environmental science laboratory. A professor is describing a water-testing project.
sentences: We collect samples from the river weekly.
Label each bottle with the date and place.
The samples must be kept cold until they reach the laboratory.
Measure the temperature and acidity of the water first.
Record each measurement carefully in your field notebook.
Because the instruments are sensitive, carry them in the protective case.
If the readings differ greatly from last week's results, repeat the test again.

title: Teaching assistant duties
scenario: You are a teaching assistant for an introductory economics course. The instructor is explaining your duties.
sentences: Please arrive ten minutes before class.
Hand out the problem sets at the door.
Students often ask what the final exam will cover.
Direct those questions to me instead of answering them yourself.
Weekly tutorials are held on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
Please explain to students that late assignments lose ten percent for each day.
At the end of the semester, you will help organize the final projects.
